title: StoryEvent has no forward-compat gate: a new event variant makes older readers fail the whole repo

description:
## What

`StoryEvent` (`src/domain.rs:179-181`) is an internally-tagged serde enum with no
unknown-variant tolerance. Adding any new event variant is therefore a **silent
breaking change to the on-disk format**: every reader built before the variant
existed fails hard, and it fails for the *whole repo*, not just the story that
carries the new event.

This is not hypothetical — it took the web dashboard down for StoryHook's own
repo on 2026-07-25.

## Why it breaks

`read_story_events()` (`src/storage.rs:721-733`) deserializes each JSONL line with
`serde_json::from_str` and propagates the first error with `?`. An unknown `kind`
tag aborts the read of that story; callers that walk every story (report building,
`story list`, the dashboard's `build_report_data`) abort the entire traversal.

There is no `#[serde(other)]` fallback, no catch-all variant, and no schema-version
field in the log that would let an old reader detect "this repo is newer than me"
and say so.

## Extent

`StoryDescriptionSet` landed in c25be1d (2026-07-23, shipped in v0.17.0). Eight
stories — [[SH-46]] through [[SH-53]] — now carry that event.

The long-lived dashboard daemon had been running since 2026-07-24 00:07 on a
pre-c25be1d build. Result: `GET /api/repos` reported

    storyhook | available: false
      unknown variant `StoryDescriptionSet`, expected one of `StoryCreated`,
      `StoryCommentAdded`, ... `StoryDeleted` at line 1 column 29

and the dashboard rendered StoryHook as a dimmed, dashed "(unavailable)" card
(`src/web_dashboard.html:2109`). Every other registered repo loaded fine — they
had no `StoryDescriptionSet` events yet.

`build_repos_json` (`src/web.rs:363-388`) did its job: it isolated the failure to
one card rather than failing the whole request. The defect is upstream of that.

Blast radius beyond this incident:

- Any long-running `story web --serve` outlives a version bump — the daemon does
  not reload its binary.
- Any collaborator or CI runner on an older build sees the repo as broken.
- Rollback to a previous release makes previously-readable repos unreadable.

## Repro

1. Check out a commit before c25be1d and `cargo build --release`.
2. Point that binary at a repo containing a `StoryDescriptionSet` event:

       ./target/release/story list

Expect a hard failure naming the unknown variant, with no stories listed —
including the ones that contain no new events at all.

## Last known good

Every release before v0.17.0 could read every log written by every earlier
release, because no variant had been added since the format stabilized. c25be1d
is the first variant addition to expose the gap; the gap itself has existed since
the enum was introduced.

## Fix

The tension: silently ignoring unknown events renders *wrong* state (a story
showing a stale description as though it were current), which is worse than
rendering none. So a bare `#[serde(other)]` catch-all is the wrong fix.

Options, best first:

1. **Schema version in the log + explicit refusal.** Record the writer's format
   version (per-repo or per-story-header). A reader that finds a version it does
   not understand fails with "this repo was written by story >= X, upgrade to
   read it" — actionable, honest, and it names the real problem instead of
   leaking a serde error to the UI.
2. **Per-story quarantine.** Have `read_story_events` collect unreadable stories
   instead of aborting the traversal, so one future-versioned story degrades to
   an explicit "unreadable" row and the rest of the repo still loads. Complements
   option 1 rather than replacing it.
3. **Unknown-variant capture with a poisoned-snapshot flag.** Deserialize unknown
   events into a catch-all that marks the folded snapshot "incomplete", so state
   is never presented as authoritative when events were skipped. More work, and
   only worth it if partial reads turn out to be genuinely useful.

Whatever ships needs a regression test that pins the compatibility contract:
a fixture log containing an unknown `kind` must produce the chosen behavior,
not a raw serde error.

## Preventative action

The defect class is "on-disk format changed without a compatibility gate." A
variant addition currently looks like an ordinary feature commit. Consider a test
that asserts the set of known `kind` tags against a checked-in golden list, so
adding a variant forces a deliberate update and a compatibility decision.

## Related

Operationally adjacent, not the same defect: the dashboard daemon does not
restart itself on upgrade, which is what let a stale reader persist for 42 hours.
Worth its own story if it recurs.
